purpose: Working inventory of TODO comments in the Porytiles2 codebase that are being systematically converted into GitHub issues. Workflow: walk the entries in strict ascending `index` order, propose an issue title/body/label for each, get user approval, file via `gh issue create` (assignee `grunt-lucas`), remove the TODO comment from the source file, then prune the entry from this JSON. The `index` field is the original ordering from the initial scan and is stable across the run; entries already filed have been deleted, so the smallest remaining index is the next entry to process. Issue body style: no `## Section` markdown headers, no semantic line breaks (single-line paragraphs), free-flow prose with bullet lists introduced by lead-ins like `Concretely:` or `Acceptance criteria:`. Per project policy, ignore Porytiles1 entirely; only Porytiles2 TODOs are in scope. When a TODO seems trivial, audit whether its premise still holds against the current codebase before filing (some TODOs are inside dead code, contradict newer conventions, or are subsumed by design docs in Porytiles2/Notes/). Issues filed during the current run so far: #203-#213. To resume, read the first entry in the `TODOs` array and continue from there.
